title: Deduplicate locally executed path mapped spawns

timeline.body:
When path mapping is enabled, different `Spawn`s in the same build can have identical `RemoteAction.ActionKey`s and can thus provide remote cache hits for each other. However, cache hits are only possible after the first local execution has concluded and uploaded its result to the cache. 

To avoid unnecessary duplication of local work, the first `Spawn` for each `RemoteAction.ActionKey` is tracked until its results have been uploaded and all other concurrently scheduled `Spawn`s wait for it and then copy over its local outputs. 

Fixes #21043
Add a comment explaining what motivates this.
I think it's worth adding a comment here explaining why this only applies to local executions - for remote executions, we rely on the remote service to deduplicate for us.
It's a little surprising for a method called `shouldFoo` to have side effects. Can you come up with a better name? Also amend the description to reflect what happens when `execution != null`.
Add a `@return` clause to the javadoc, documenting in particular the meaning of `null`.

I think we should only fail if the output is considered mandatory for the current spawn (compare with https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/RemoteExecutionService.java;l=1292;drc=a804fb1748ce767d98f8b7a40e660ed22576e30e).

The `FileOutErr` is action-scoped, not spawn-scoped (see https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/AbstractSpawnStrategy.java;l=363;drc=d32202b20f82c17f75ee204d505b08f2160640f5), so I think this might incorrectly replay output unrelated to this spawn? Should we first introduce a separate Spawn-scoped `OutErr`?

reply.body: This is correct, but I think that the distinction ends up not mattering for the path mapping use case. I added a comment explaining this, please let me know what you think.
I think this is good enough for now, thanks.

timeline.body: Nit: for consistency with other usages, let's call this `previousExecution`.

FYI - I suspect that this has a chance of failing if we ever apply path mapping to test actions with multiple test attempts (which move spawn outputs to a different location after spawn execution). This is already a problem for async uploading, so whatever we end up doing to fix it should also apply here. No need to do anything about it for now.

reply.body: That's a good catch. At least in its current form, path mapping for test actions wouldn't be very useful as top-level targets that differ in configuration typically do so intentionally, with at least some part of their transitive closure being different (as in, different file content). In this case, path mapping wouldn't help.

timeline.body: I think it would be preferable to test all of the different scenarios here and keep just the shell test for the success case, as Java tests are much faster than shell tests.

reply.body: The failing tests verify some tricky aspects (e.g. WARNING instead of INFO output), but I will try and see whether I manage to convert them. Being able to run them faster would indeed be very useful.
I added Java tests for the same scenarios covered in the shell tests. Should I delete all shell tests for failing scenarios?
I'm happy with the current state.

+function test_path_stripping_cache_hit_for_parallel_action() {
+  if is_windows; then
+    echo "Skipping test_path_stripping_singleplex_worker on Windows as it requires sandboxing"
+    return
+  fi
+
+  mkdir rules
+  touch rules/BUILD
+  cat > rules/defs.bzl <<'EOF'
+def _slow_write_impl(ctx):
+    out = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.attr.name)
+    args = ctx.actions.args().add(out)
+    ctx.actions.run_shell(
+         outputs = [out],
+         command = "sleep 2 && echo 'echo \"Hello, World!\"' > $1",
+         arguments = [args],
+         execution_requirements = {"supports-path-mapping": ""},
+    )
+    return [
+        DefaultInfo(executable = out),
+    ]
+
+slow_write = rule(_slow_write_impl)
+EOF
+
+  mkdir -p pkg
+  cat > pkg/BUILD <<'EOF'
+load("//rules:defs.bzl", "slow_write")
+
+slow_write(name = "script")
+
+genrule(
+    name = "gen_exec",
+    outs = ["out_exec"],
+    cmd = "$(location :script) > $@",
+    tools = [":script"],
+)
+
+genrule(
+    name = "gen_target",
+    outs = ["out_target"],
+    cmd = "$(location :script) > $@",
+    srcs = [":script"],
+)
+EOF
+
+  bazel build \
+    --experimental_output_paths=strip \
+    --remote_cache=grpc://localhost:${worker_port} \
+    //pkg:all &> $TEST_log || fail "build failed unexpectedly"
+  # The first slow_write action plus two genrules.
+  expect_log '3 \(linux\|darwin\|processwrapper\)-sandbox'
+  expect_log '1 concurrent execution cache hit'
+}
+
 run_suite "path mapping tests"
